blocks.text: iOS 7 replaced the system’s visual language and paired that redesign with Control Center, a Today view in Notification Center, more capable multitasking, AirDrop, reorganized Photos, a revised Camera, and a streamlined Safari experience.

citations.locator: iOS 7 — New design through Safari improvements

blocks.text: The release also introduced iTunes Radio, expanded Siri and App Store behavior, added Activation Lock and FaceTime Audio, broadened accessibility and device-management tools, and shipped a large security repair set covering data protection, networking, the kernel, Safari, and WebKit.

citations.locator: iOS 7 — iTunes Radio through Education features

blocks.text: Apple’s surviving release history describes iOS 7.0.1 only as a package of bug fixes and improvements for iPhone 5c and iPhone 5s. It does not enumerate the corrected behaviors or identify a separate security delta.
iOS 7.0.2 focused on lock-screen protections. Apple documented separate paths that could expose dialing controls or recently used apps and photos while a device was locked.
The update also restored the Greek keyboard as a passcode-entry option. Apple’s 2013 security index records the release on September 26, 2013.

iOS 7.0.3 introduced iCloud Keychain and Safari password generation, restored web and Wikipedia results in Spotlight, and repaired iMessage sending and activation along with several stability, sensor, speech, accessibility, and device-supervision problems.
It also refined Touch ID behavior at the lock screen and closed three documented physical-access paths involving the passcode view, emergency dialing, and the Phone app’s Contacts pane.

citations.locator: iOS 7.0.3 — Touch ID and Lock screen

blocks.text: iOS 7.0.4 was a focused maintenance release that corrected FaceTime calls failing for some users and otherwise carried general bug fixes and improvements.
Its dedicated security advisory documents an App Store authorization correction that enforced the password prompt before an app or in-app purchase could complete.
iOS 7.0.6 was a security-specific update for SSL connection verification rather than a feature release.

Apple’s advisory explains that Secure Transport had omitted validation steps, allowing a suitably positioned network attacker to capture or alter data in protected sessions; the update restored those checks.
iOS 7.1 introduced CarPlay and expanded Siri, iTunes Radio, Calendar, accessibility, Camera, iCloud Keychain, and cross-device FaceTime behavior.

It also improved Touch ID recognition and iPhone 4 performance, continued interface refinements, corrected several reliability issues, and delivered a broad security set spanning device boundaries, document and image parsing, networking, the kernel, Safari, and WebKit.

citations.locator: CarPlay availability as an iOS 7 update

blocks.text: iOS 7.1.1 further improved Touch ID recognition and corrected keyboard responsiveness and Bluetooth-keyboard behavior when VoiceOver was enabled.
The security update also repaired incomplete HTTP header handling, kernel-pointer exposure, an SSL renegotiation weakness, and multiple WebKit memory-corruption issues.

citations.locator: CFNetwork HTTPProtocol, IOKit Kernel, Secure Transport, and WebKit entries

blocks.text: iOS 7.1.2 improved iBeacon connectivity and stability, repaired data transfer for some third-party accessories such as barcode scanners, and corrected the data-protection class used for Mail attachments.

Its security bulletin also records fixes for Activation Lock, lock-screen limits, Find My iPhone, Siri contact exposure, launchd privilege flaws, Safari and WebKit content handling, certificate policy, and kernel reliability.

events.summary: The public iOS 7 release combined a system-wide redesign with new quick controls, background behavior, sharing, media, security, accessibility, and administration capabilities.

blocks.text: The most visible change was structural rather than cosmetic alone: Apple rebuilt the interface around new typography, color, translucency, and motion while adding Control Center and a lock-screen-accessible Notification Center with a Today view.

citations.locator: iOS 7 — New design, Control Center, and Notification Center
Redesigned interface, Control Center, and Notification Center

blocks.text: Under that surface, iOS 7 expanded multitasking and nearby sharing, reorganized photos, modernized Safari and Siri, added Activation Lock and FaceTime Audio, and introduced new accessibility, enterprise, and education controls alongside extensive security fixes.

changes.title: System-wide visual redesign
changes.canonicalSummary: iOS 7 replaced the system interface with a new visual structure built around refined typography, color, translucency, layers, and motion.
changes.summary: Apple applied the redesigned presentation across the operating system and built-in apps, including new sounds and visual depth effects.

changes.title: Control Center and expanded Notification Center
changes.canonicalSummary: Quick settings moved into a new bottom-edge Control Center while Notification Center gained lock-screen access and a Today view.
changes.summary: Control Center exposed common radios, brightness, media, AirPlay, AirDrop, and utility shortcuts; Notification Center summarized the day and synchronized dismissed notices across devices.

citations.locator: iOS 7 — Control Center and Notification Center improvements

changes.title: Visual multitasking and background updates
changes.canonicalSummary: The app switcher gained visual previews and apps could refresh content in the background under the new multitasking model.
changes.summary: Users could move among preview cards, while supported apps could keep information current without remaining in the foreground.

changes.title: Reworked Camera and Photos workflows
changes.canonicalSummary: Camera added swipeable modes and live filters, while Photos organized media by time and place and expanded shared-stream collaboration.
changes.summary: The update introduced square capture and real-time filters on supported devices, Moments-based organization, video-capable iCloud Photo Sharing, and a shared activity view.

changes.title: AirDrop nearby sharing
changes.canonicalSummary: AirDrop added encrypted peer-to-peer content transfer between supported nearby Apple devices.
changes.summary: The sharing workflow discovered nearby recipients and transferred selected content without requiring a conventional network setup.

changes.title: Safari, Siri, and iTunes Radio expansion
changes.canonicalSummary: Safari and Siri gained new discovery and navigation tools, and iTunes Radio introduced personalized streaming stations in its launch markets.
changes.summary: Safari combined search and addresses and added new tab and shared-link views; Siri gained new voices, integrated reference and web results, and settings control; iTunes Radio offered curated and user-created stations.

citations.locator: iOS 7 — Safari, iTunes Radio, and Siri improvements

changes.title: App Store discovery and automatic updates
changes.canonicalSummary: The App Store added location-aware and children’s discovery areas and could update installed apps automatically.
changes.summary: Popular Near Me surfaced locally relevant apps, a Kids category organized age-appropriate software, and automatic updating reduced manual maintenance.

changes.title: Activation Lock and communication controls
changes.canonicalSummary: Activation Lock tied sensitive Find My iPhone actions to an Apple ID password, while iOS added FaceTime Audio and contact blocking.
changes.summary: The release required account authentication for disabling Find My iPhone, erasing or reactivating a device, and signing out of iCloud; it also added data-based FaceTime calls and blocking across Phone, Messages, and FaceTime.

citations.locator: iOS 7 — Find My iPhone Activation Lock and communication features

changes.title: Expanded accessibility controls
changes.canonicalSummary: iOS 7 added Switch Control and broadened VoiceOver, caption, Braille, hearing-aid, and single-app accessibility options.
changes.summary: Users gained switch-based device control, customizable captions, VoiceOver handwriting and Nemeth Braille output, premium speech voices, and expanded hearing-aid support on compatible hardware.

changes.title: Enterprise and education management expansion
changes.canonicalSummary: Managed app, account, network, enrollment, filtering, and classroom display controls were expanded for organizations.
changes.summary: The release added managed open-in rules, per-app VPN, enterprise single sign-on, remote managed-app configuration, streamlined MDM enrollment, web filtering, and additional AirPlay classroom controls.

changes.title: Security foundation repairs
changes.canonicalSummary: The iOS 7 security bulletin documents repairs across trust, data protection, media parsing, process boundaries, networking, the kernel, Safari, and WebKit.
changes.summary: Representative fixes tightened passcode-attempt enforcement, prevented background apps from injecting interface events, corrected several kernel and content-processing defects, and addressed browser memory-safety issues.

citations.locator: Data Protection, IOKit, Kernel, Safari, and WebKit entries

events.summary: iOS 7.0.1 was a device-specific maintenance update for iPhone 5c and iPhone 5s, but Apple’s surviving notes do not itemize the underlying fixes.

blocks.text: The historical record is deliberately sparse for this release. Apple limits the description to bug fixes and improvements, identifies iPhone 5c and iPhone 5s as the applicable devices, and records both iTunes and over-the-air distribution.

changes.title: Device-specific maintenance update
changes.canonicalSummary: Apple documented a general package of fixes and improvements limited to iPhone 5c and iPhone 5s without itemizing the changes.
changes.summary: The surviving first-party note confirms the update’s maintenance purpose and device scope, but does not support attributing any particular corrected symptom.

events.summary: iOS 7.0.2 closed two documented lock-screen access paths and restored Greek keyboard support for passcode entry.

blocks.text: The security work addressed two different lock-screen state failures: one could make the dialer treat a restarting lock screen as unlocked, while another could expose recent apps and permit Camera access to photos during certain transitions.
Alongside those restrictions, Apple reintroduced a Greek keyboard choice for entering a passcode, making this a small release with both security and input-language consequences.

changes.title: Lock-screen dialer restriction
changes.canonicalSummary: A lock-screen restart no longer allowed the call dialer to treat the device as unlocked and place non-emergency calls.
changes.summary: Apple avoided the null dereference that could occur after repeated emergency-button taps and lead the dialer to accept arbitrary numbers during the restart.

changes.title: Lock-screen app and photo access restriction
changes.canonicalSummary: A locked-device transition no longer exposed recently used apps or allowed Camera access to view, edit, or share photos.
changes.summary: Apple corrected the transition handling that could reveal the recent-app list and open Camera while the device remained locked.

changes.title: Greek passcode keyboard restored
changes.canonicalSummary: Greek keyboard input returned as an option on the passcode screen.
changes.summary: The update restored a previously available Greek keyboard choice specifically for passcode entry.

events.summary: iOS 7.0.3 added iCloud Keychain and password generation, restored Spotlight web search, improved reliability and accessibility, and tightened lock-screen handling.

blocks.text: The release’s main new capability was credential management: approved devices could synchronize account names, passwords, and payment-card details through iCloud Keychain, while Safari could suggest stronger unique passwords.

citations.locator: iOS 7.0.3 — iCloud Keychain and Password Generator

blocks.text: A wider maintenance pass restored Spotlight web sources, repaired iMessage activation and sending, improved motion and VoiceOver behavior, preserved supervised-device status, and corrected three lock-screen or Phone-state weaknesses documented by Apple.

changes.title: iCloud Keychain and password generation
changes.canonicalSummary: iCloud Keychain synchronized saved credentials and payment-card details across approved devices, and Safari could propose unique passwords.
changes.summary: Users gained an Apple-managed credential store shared among approved devices plus an integrated generator for harder-to-guess website passwords.

citations.locator: iOS 7.0.3 — iCloud Keychain and Password Generator

changes.title: Spotlight web and reference search restored
changes.canonicalSummary: Spotlight again offered searches of the web and Wikipedia from the system search interface.
changes.summary: The update restored external web and reference lookup choices that were absent from the initial iOS 7 release.

changes.title: iMessage sending and activation reliability
changes.canonicalSummary: Apple corrected failures that could prevent iMessage activation or stop messages from sending for some users.
changes.summary: The maintenance work covered both account activation and message delivery paths for affected iMessage users.

changes.title: System, sensor, and voice reliability
changes.canonicalSummary: The release improved iWork stability, accelerometer calibration, and the voice quality used by Siri and VoiceOver.
changes.summary: Apple addressed crashes or instability around iWork apps, corrected a calibration error in motion sensing, and fixed a fallback to lower-quality synthesized speech.

citations.locator: iOS 7.0.3 — iWork, accelerometer, Siri, and VoiceOver fixes

changes.title: Accessibility and supervised-device behavior
changes.canonicalSummary: Reduce Motion, VoiceOver input, Bold Text, and supervised-device upgrade behavior received targeted corrections.
changes.summary: Motion reduction expanded to cover animation as well as movement, VoiceOver input sensitivity was adjusted, Bold Text reached dial-pad text, and updates no longer removed supervision from affected devices.

citations.locator: iOS 7.0.3 — Reduce Motion, VoiceOver, Bold Text, and supervised devices

changes.title: Touch ID lock-screen timing
changes.canonicalSummary: The lock screen delayed the slide-to-unlock prompt while Touch ID authentication was active.
changes.summary: This presentation change kept the legacy unlock prompt from appearing immediately when a user was authenticating with Touch ID.

changes.title: Lock-screen and Phone protections
changes.canonicalSummary: Three physical-access paths involving emergency calls, passcode retry timing, and locked-device contacts were closed.
changes.summary: Apple prevented arbitrary dialing during a lock-screen restart, restored enforcement of incorrect-passcode delays after returning from Phone, and blocked the Phone app’s Contacts pane while locked.

citations.locator: Passcode Lock — CVE-2013-5144 and CVE-2013-5162; Phone — CVE-2013-5164

events.summary: iOS 7.0.4 repaired FaceTime call failures and strengthened App Store purchase authorization, alongside unspecified maintenance improvements.

blocks.text: The user-facing note singles out FaceTime reliability: the update fixed a condition that prevented calls from completing for some people, while leaving the rest of the maintenance package undescribed.

Apple separately documented an App Store authorization flaw in which a signed-in user could complete a prompted transaction without supplying the requested password; additional checks enforced that authorization step.

changes.title: FaceTime call reliability
changes.canonicalSummary: A FaceTime failure that affected call completion for some users was corrected.
changes.summary: Apple identified FaceTime call failure as the specific user-facing repair in this otherwise general maintenance update.

changes.title: App Store purchase authorization
changes.canonicalSummary: App and in-app purchases could no longer complete through the affected path without satisfying a displayed password requirement.
changes.summary: Additional purchase-authorization enforcement prevented a signed-in user from bypassing the password prompt during a transaction.

events.summary: iOS 7.0.6 restored missing SSL/TLS authenticity checks in Secure Transport, closing a documented network interception and modification risk.

blocks.text: This release had one documented purpose: repair SSL connection verification. Apple’s security bulletin identifies missing authenticity-validation steps in Secure Transport rather than a collection of unrelated feature or maintenance changes.

The affected condition required an attacker with a privileged network position and could expose protected sessions to captured or modified data. Restoring the omitted validation steps addressed that path.

changes.title: Secure Transport certificate validation
changes.canonicalSummary: Secure Transport restored missing connection-authenticity checks for SSL/TLS sessions.
changes.summary: The repair prevented the documented privileged-network attack path from capturing or changing data by reinstating validation steps that had not been performed.

events.summary: iOS 7.1 introduced CarPlay, expanded Siri, media, calendar, and accessibility controls, improved performance and reliability, and delivered extensive security repairs.

blocks.text: CarPlay was the defining new platform feature, projecting selected Phone, Music, Maps, Messages, and compatible audio-app experiences into supported vehicles with Siri and the vehicle’s own controls.

citations.locator: CarPlay functions, controls, compatibility, and availability

blocks.text: The same release refined Siri listening and voices, iTunes Radio, Calendar, visual accessibility, Camera, Keychain, FaceTime notifications, Touch ID, and iPhone 4 performance, while Apple’s security bulletin records fixes across local, network, content, and browser attack surfaces.

citations.locator: iOS 7.1 — Siri through continued user interface refinements
CarPlay availability as an iOS 7 update

changes.title: CarPlay
changes.canonicalSummary: CarPlay brought selected iPhone communication, navigation, media, messaging, and third-party audio experiences to compatible vehicle interfaces.
changes.summary: A Lightning-enabled compatible iPhone could connect to a supported vehicle and expose Phone, Maps, Messages, Music, and selected audio apps through Siri, touch, knobs, buttons, or steering-wheel voice control.

citations.locator: CarPlay capabilities, controls, compatible iPhones, and availability

changes.title: Siri listening control and voices
changes.canonicalSummary: Siri added push-to-talk listening control and new natural-sounding voice options in several language variants.
changes.summary: Holding the Home button let a user determine exactly when Siri listened, and additional male and female voices arrived for Mandarin Chinese, UK English, Australian English, and Japanese.

changes.title: iTunes Radio discovery and purchasing
changes.canonicalSummary: iTunes Radio gained easier station creation, album purchasing from Now Playing, and on-device iTunes Match subscription.
changes.summary: A search field supported station creation from an artist or song, albums could be bought directly from the playback view, and users could subscribe to iTunes Match for ad-free listening.

changes.title: Calendar month events and holidays
changes.canonicalSummary: Calendar could display events in month view and automatically include country- or region-specific holidays in supported locations.
changes.summary: The month presentation gained visible events, while holiday calendars were added automatically for many countries and regions.

changes.title: Accessibility display and motion controls
changes.canonicalSummary: Bold Text and Reduce Motion covered more of the interface, and new controls exposed button shapes, darker colors, and reduced white point.
changes.summary: Bold styling extended to the keyboard, calculator, and icons; motion reduction reached Weather, Messages, and multitasking; and additional visual contrast controls became available.

changes.title: Camera, Keychain, and FaceTime refinements
changes.canonicalSummary: The update added automatic HDR on iPhone 5s, expanded iCloud Keychain availability, and synchronized answered-call notifications across FaceTime devices.
changes.summary: A new Camera setting could enable HDR automatically on iPhone 5s, more countries and regions received iCloud Keychain, and answering a FaceTime call elsewhere cleared the corresponding notification.

citations.locator: iOS 7.1 — Camera, iCloud Keychain, and FaceTime

changes.title: Touch ID, performance, and reliability improvements
changes.canonicalSummary: Fingerprint recognition, iPhone 4 performance, home-screen stability, large Mail badges, and interface details received maintenance work.
changes.summary: Apple improved Touch ID matching and iPhone 4 performance, repaired an occasional home-screen crash and Mail unread counts above 10,000, and continued general interface refinements.

citations.locator: iOS 7.1 — Touch ID through continued user interface refinements

changes.title: Device-boundary protections
changes.canonicalSummary: The release tightened access to FaceTime contacts, cross-app input observation, Find My iPhone settings, and pre-activation home-screen state.
changes.summary: Apple blocked a failed lock-screen FaceTime call from exposing contacts, restricted IOKit monitoring of actions in other apps, required improved Find My iPhone state handling, and hardened activation error handling.

citations.locator: FaceTime — CVE-2014-1274; IOKit HID Event — CVE-2014-1276; Settings - Accounts — CVE-2014-2019; Springboard — CVE-2014-1285

changes.title: Content parsing and kernel security
changes.canonicalSummary: Multiple image, document, and kernel flaws that could disclose data, crash the device, or permit code execution were corrected.
changes.summary: Representative repairs added validation or safer memory handling for JPEG2000, TIFF, JPEG, and Word content and fixed an out-of-bounds kernel memory access path.

citations.locator: ImageIO, Kernel, and Office Viewer entries

changes.title: Store and Safari transport protections
changes.canonicalSummary: Enterprise app delivery and Safari credential autofill received stronger transport and origin checks.
changes.summary: Enterprise App Download added SSL use and redirect prompts to reduce spoofed delivery, while Safari tracked frame origins more carefully before autofilling site credentials.

events.summary: iOS 7.1.1 refined Touch ID, fixed keyboard and VoiceOver interactions, and addressed network-session, kernel-information, and WebKit security issues.

blocks.text: The user-facing maintenance work centered on input: fingerprint matching received another refinement, software-keyboard responsiveness was repaired, and Bluetooth keyboards no longer hit the documented problem when VoiceOver was active.

Apple’s security bulletin adds four areas not visible in the consumer summary: incomplete cookie headers, exposed kernel pointers, SSL renegotiation, and malicious web content each received targeted defenses.

citations.locator: CFNetwork HTTPProtocol, IOKit Kernel, Secure Transport, and WebKit entries

changes.title: Touch ID recognition
changes.canonicalSummary: Fingerprint recognition received an additional accuracy and reliability improvement.
changes.summary: Apple described this as a further refinement to Touch ID matching rather than a new enrollment or authentication workflow.

changes.title: Keyboard responsiveness
changes.canonicalSummary: A defect that could make the on-screen keyboard respond poorly was corrected.
changes.summary: The update targeted responsiveness of keyboard input without documenting a narrower trigger or affected-app list.

changes.title: VoiceOver with Bluetooth keyboards
changes.canonicalSummary: A compatibility problem involving Bluetooth keyboards while VoiceOver was enabled was fixed.
changes.summary: The release restored the affected assistive-technology and hardware-keyboard interaction documented in Apple’s consumer notes.

changes.title: HTTP cookie and SSL session security
changes.canonicalSummary: Network handling was tightened for incomplete cookie headers and a Secure Transport renegotiation scenario.
changes.summary: CFNetwork ignored incomplete HTTP header lines so truncated cookie security attributes could not be stripped, and Secure Transport required renegotiated sessions to retain the original server certificate by default.

citations.locator: CFNetwork HTTPProtocol — CVE-2014-1296; Secure Transport — CVE-2014-1295

changes.title: Kernel information and WebKit memory safety
changes.canonicalSummary: The update removed exposed kernel pointers from an IOKit object and corrected multiple WebKit memory-corruption flaws.
changes.summary: Removing the pointers reduced a path for bypassing kernel address randomization, while improved WebKit memory handling addressed malicious-content crash or code-execution risks.

events.summary: iOS 7.1.2 improved iBeacon and accessory communication, protected Mail attachments correctly, and closed a broad set of device, process, browser, and trust weaknesses.

blocks.text: The visible maintenance work focused on nearby and attached hardware: iBeacon behavior became more stable, and a transfer defect affecting some third-party accessories, including barcode scanners, was corrected.

The update also changed Mail attachment encryption and carried a substantial security set spanning activation and lock-screen boundaries, system-service memory safety, browser content, trust policy, and kernel input validation.

citations.locator: Mail, Lockdown, Lock Screen, launchd, Safari, WebKit, Certificate Trust Policy, and Kernel entries

changes.title: iBeacon connectivity and stability
changes.canonicalSummary: iBeacon connections received reliability and stability improvements.
changes.summary: Apple identified more dependable iBeacon behavior as one of the three principal user-facing changes in iOS 7.1.2.

changes.title: Third-party accessory data transfer
changes.canonicalSummary: A transfer defect affecting some external accessories, including barcode scanners, was corrected.
changes.summary: The update repaired communication with a subset of third-party accessory hardware rather than changing the overall accessory model.

changes.title: Mail attachment data protection
changes.canonicalSummary: Mail attachments used the corrected encryption class so they received the intended at-rest data protection.
changes.summary: Apple changed the attachment encryption class after documenting that physical access could expose Mail attachments on iPhone 4 under the affected configuration.

changes.title: Activation, lock-screen, account, and Siri boundaries
changes.canonicalSummary: The update strengthened Activation Lock, passcode retry enforcement, foreground-app isolation, Find My iPhone state, and locked-device Siri contact access.
changes.summary: Additional checks and state handling reduced partial Activation Lock bypass, enforced failed-passcode limits, protected the prior foreground app, required proper Find My iPhone authorization, and gated Siri’s complete contact list behind the passcode.

citations.locator: Lockdown — CVE-2014-1360; Lock Screen — CVE-2014-1352 and CVE-2014-1353; Settings — CVE-2014-1350; Siri — CVE-2014-1351

changes.title: launchd privilege safeguards
changes.canonicalSummary: Four launchd integer and heap-boundary flaws that could allow system-privileged code execution were corrected.
changes.summary: Improved bounds checking addressed IPC-message and log-message heap overflows together with integer overflow and underflow paths in the system service manager.

changes.title: Safari and WebKit content security
changes.canonicalSummary: Safari and WebKit received memory, origin, and URL-display corrections for malicious web content.
changes.summary: Apple fixed a Safari use-after-free, multiple WebKit memory-corruption issues, a postMessage origin-encoding flaw, and an address-bar domain-spoofing condition.

citations.locator: Safari — CVE-2014-1349; WebKit — CVE-2014-1345, CVE-2014-1346, and listed memory-corruption entries

changes.title: Certificate trust and kernel validation
changes.canonicalSummary: Certificate trust policy was updated and an IOKit argument-validation defect that could restart the device was repaired.
changes.summary: The release revised the trusted-certificate policy and added validation for IOKit API arguments that could otherwise trigger a kernel null-pointer dereference and unexpected restart.
